classification.difficultyReason: Track vertices through two turns using the circular grid, preserve their radii, and combine directed angles even when the first image coincides with the original.

inlines.text: Carry out the rotation given for each figure, draw the image, and then carry out the second rotation. Find a single rotation that will have the same effect.

spec.description: Five concentric circles with unit descriptive spacing, rays every 30 degrees and a square boundary. The original triangle has vertices at descriptive polar positions (2,0°), (5,0°), (4,30°). No numerical polar labels are printed.
spec.mathematics: Rotate every vertex about the marked centre while preserving its radius.

answer.worked:
Rotate each vertex two $30^\circ$ divisions anticlockwise and join the images. Then rotate those vertices one further division anticlockwise and join them. Each vertex stays on its original circle.

$$60^\circ+30^\circ=90^\circ.$$

The single rotation is $90^\circ$ anticlockwise about the marked centre. In the diagram, blue is the original, red is the first image and green is the final image.

spec.description: Complete scaffold with original triangle, dashed first image rotated 60 degrees anticlockwise, and final image rotated 90 degrees anticlockwise from the original.
spec.mathematics: First-image polar angles are 60°, 60°, 90°; final-image angles are 90°, 90°, 120°, retaining respective radii 2, 5, 4.

spec.description: Five-circle polar scaffold and four-sided figure. Boundary vertices have descriptive polar positions (3,60°), (5,45°), (3,30°), (2,45°). The two 45-degree vertices lie between the printed rays; no additional rays or polar labels are added.
spec.mathematics: All four vertices rotate about the marked centre with their radii preserved.

answer.worked:
Rotate each vertex one $30^\circ$ division anticlockwise and join the images. Then rotate the first image two divisions clockwise, keeping each vertex the same distance from the centre.

The second turn reverses the first $30^\circ$ and continues a further $30^\circ$ clockwise. The single rotation is therefore $30^\circ$ clockwise about the marked centre.

In the diagram, blue is the original, red is the first image and green is the final image.

spec.description: Complete scaffold with original quadrilateral, dashed first image at +30 degrees, and final image at -30 degrees relative to the original.
spec.mathematics: First-image boundary angles are 90°, 75°, 60°, 75°; final-image angles are 30°, 15°, 0°, 15°, retaining radii 3, 5, 3, 2.

spec.description: Five-circle polar scaffold with equilateral triangle on the third circle, at descriptive angles 90, 210 and 330 degrees. No numerical labels are printed.
spec.mathematics: The first 120-degree rotation permutes the vertices; the outline coincides with the original.

answer.short:
$210^\circ$ anticlockwise about the marked centre.

The first image coincides with the original triangle.
answer.worked:
Rotate each vertex four $30^\circ$ divisions anticlockwise. The vertices exchange positions, so the first image has the same outline as the original triangle. Rotate that image a further three divisions anticlockwise.

$$120^\circ+90^\circ=210^\circ.$$

The single rotation is $210^\circ$ anticlockwise about the marked centre. The dashed red first image coincides with the blue original; green shows the final image.

spec.description: Complete scaffold. The first 120-degree image coincides with the original equilateral triangle; a dashed stroke preserves this relationship. The final image is rotated 210 degrees from the original.
spec.mathematics: First-image vertices occupy angles 210°, 330°, 90°; final vertices occupy 300°, 60°, 180°, all at radius 3.
